items.t: Said his goal is to run secure, fair and accurate elections and that the voter record cleanup will strengthen voter rolls.
items.q: From day one, our goal was clear: run elections that are secure, fair, and accurate. This move will strengthen our voter rolls and reinforce public trust in our elections.

items.t: Said that when he ran for Oregon Secretary of State, he promised to improve how Oregon audits state government and restore trust in the process.
items.q: When I ran for Oregon Secretary of State, I promised to improve how Oregon audits state government and restore trust in our process,”

items.t: Says his first priority as Secretary of State is to hold the state accountable for delivering on its promises and managing tax dollars wisely.
items.q: As Secretary of State, Tobias' first priority is to hold the State of Oregon accountable for delivering on its promises, managing tax dollars wisely, and running secure, fair elections.

record.t: Was elected Oregon state representative in 2006.
record.q: He worked at the U.S. Treasury and Nike, Inc. prior to his election as state representative in 2006 and state treasurer in 2016.

record.t: Serves as Oregon's 30th secretary of state.
record.q: Tobias Read is Oregon’s 30th secretary of state.

record.t: Announced two directives that he said will restart routine cleanup of outdated, inactive voter registration records.

record.q: The first directive orders counties to immediately cancel long-inactive voter registrations that already met the legal requirements for removal before 2017.

record.t: Said he was sponsoring bills with colleagues related to Oregonians' retirement.
